evidence: A calculation on products: the design climate's fifteen settled years (an estimate carried by pattern scaling to 300.31 K and then onto the design's own surface), each routed on the design routing's structure held fixed, the lakes as the corrected rule fills them, without storage and with the lakes and the upper seas carrying their volume from year to year over outlets sized by Earth's channel widths; the rivers' losses in the drylands by river_losses.py's estimate. Fifteen years is a short record, and no figure is validated against an observation.
reading_rule: Flows in m3/s, lengths in km, areas in km2; a year is a settled year of the design climate (model years 45-59). Each year is routed three ways: none, with no water carried between years and the lakes the design leaves below their passes passing nothing, the lower bound on a dry year's flow for the waters the design holds full; narrow and wide, with the lakes' and the upper seas' storage carried from year to year over outlets of width 3 and 15 m per (m3/s)^0.5 widened for lunar gravity, wide holding the least, a lake below its pass rising in wet years and passing water on once it reaches it. A reach is part of a major river (threshold_m3s or more on the design routing) between confluences, lakes of lake_break_km2 or more and changes of class, its flows read at its downstream end; it is sustained when it carries the threshold in every year with the wide outlets' storage and intermittent otherwise. A river is a stem from its head to where it ends or joins a larger river, classed by its end. after_losses gives the design climate's flow after the drylands' losses at the low and high ends, and lowest_year_high the wide storage's lowest year less the high end's loss of the mean year. product holds the cells, reaches the full table.
limits: The climate is an estimate in two steps: the run at sunlight 0.936 carried by pattern scaling from 301.00 K to 300.31 K, each year keeping its own departures from the run's mean, and then each cell's rain and evaporation moved by the ratio the step onto the design's own surface gives the mean (climate.gcm.surface_change, from existing runs); a run on that surface at the design temperature would differ by more than the noise of fifteen years' means where the lakes grew.

Fifteen years is a short record: the lowest year is about the driest year in fifteen and the second lowest the driest in seven or eight; longer records hold drier years, so a river sustained here can fall under the threshold in a rarer drought. The years follow one another in the model's order.

Without storage each year passes on only its own surplus: the lower bound on a dry year's flow for the waters the design holds full. With storage a lake that fell below its pass in a dry year refills before it spills again, so in the years after a drought its river can carry less than without storage (by_storage.*.km_whose_lowest_year_falls_below_none).

The storage's outlets are not designed or measured: each passes critical flow over a section as wide as Earth's alluvial channels at its design flow, at both ends of their range, so the head a lake holds over its pass, and with it the water it carries into a dry year, is an assumption; a pass the water has not cut would be wider and hold less. A lake's area over its pass is held at its area at the pass.

Each year is a year's mean rain and evaporation in 24 steps: the seasons and the storms within a year are left out, and a year's rain is resolved over the climate model's land cells of about 17,391 km2, the routing's 1.9 km cells taking it bilinearly.
The losses are river_losses.py's estimate at the ends of its ranges, taken from the mean year's flow; the lowest year after losses deducts the mean year's loss.

The structure is held fixed: the lakes keep the design's shores in the years without storage, a lake that reaches its pass with storage sends its water on by the course the design gives it and not into the larger hollow it would fill with its neighbour, and each cut carries the design's part of its branch's share whether or not its lake can spare it that year. Where the near-side sea is one sea across its neck, both parts are held at their design levels.
The routing is the design routing's on 1.9 km cells, each hollow filled as one water (lake_rule.py). Nothing is validated against an observation.

near_side.note: left: what a part receives, with the neck's flow taken from the main part and given to the southern one, beyond what it loses; the design routing settles each part within 0.2% of what it receives

land_runoff_m3s.note: the routing's runoff from the design's dry ground: each 1.9 km cell's rain less evaporation where positive, so a year wetter where that straddles nothing adds runoff and a drier one cannot take any away

routed.rule: each loss taken from the river cell it falls on (a floodplain's from the nearest river cell), never more than the cell carries, and the year routed again: a lake or sea below receives less and Moscoviense passes on less by its fixed shares

ends.low: the narrow channel and belt (width coefficient 3, belt 0.5 km)
ends.high: the wide channel and belt (15, 2 km) and the floodplains kept wet at 5 m

against_the_earlier_climate.note: [river_losses.json on the present design climate at 8 degrees with the governed routing, this estimate on the design climate with the design routing]; the connected floodplains are the earlier record's on the routing's own budget and these on the closed budget, whose routing the design routing is
